T: Genovian pears. Palate cleansers. Corn dogs.
D: A shy San Francisco teenager finds out she's the heir to the throne of the small country of Genovia.
P: Serve dessert when the sorbet arrives at the state dinner.
S: Queen Clarisse trying a corn dog
Cocktail franks dipped in a cornmeal batter, fried at 180C until golden, served with mustard and tomato sauce.
Baguette slices toasted, topped with blue cheese, thin slices of pear and a drizzle of honey.
Sourdough garlic bites with hot clam dip
Mia's home in an old San Francisco firehouse

Sourdough cubes tossed in garlic butter and toasted crisp, served with a bubbling dip of chopped clams, cream cheese, parmesan and lemon. Heat the oven to 190C. Cut half a sourdough loaf into 3cm cubes and toss with 60g melted butter mixed with 2 crushed garlic cloves and parsley. Bake 12 minutes until crisp. Beat 250g cream cheese with 2 tbsp mayo, 40g grated parmesan, the zest and juice of half a lemon and 2 sliced spring onions. Fold in 2 drained 140g tins of chopped clams. Spread into a small dish, top with more parmesan and bake 15 minutes until bubbling.
M: the state dinner where Mia learns about palate cleansers
Chicken breasts stuffed with spinach and ricotta, roasted at 200C for 20 minutes, with a lemon butter sauce and potato gratin.

Soda-battered white fish fried crisp in warm tortillas with lime slaw, pickled red onion and a chipotle crema, plenty of coriander on top. Slice 1 red onion thin and cover with 80ml lime juice and a pinch of salt for 20 minutes. Shred a quarter of a cabbage and toss with lime and salt. Mix 150g sour cream with 1 tsp chipotle in adobo. Whisk 150g plain flour, 1 tsp baking powder and 250ml cold soda water. Cut 600g flathead fillets into strips, dip in the batter and fry at 180C for 3 minutes. Warm 8 tortillas and fill with slaw, fish, onion, crema and coriander.
W: the sorbet Mia eats before she knows it's a palate cleanser
Lemon sorbet scooped into small chilled glasses with a few poached pear slices and mint.
K: Pear juice topped with sparkling water and a squeeze of lemon, over ice.

s.note: Queen Clarisse trying a corn dog
s.how: Whisk 100g cornmeal, 100g flour, a teaspoon of baking powder and 250ml buttermilk to a thick batter. Pat 24 cocktail franks dry, push a skewer into each, dip and fry at 180C for 3 minutes. Serve with mustard. A queen's first.

Slice a baguette and toast until golden. Top each with a little blue cheese and a thin slice of pear. Drizzle with honey and scatter with chopped walnuts. Serve on a silver tray, as befits a small European kingdom.

m.note: the state dinner where Mia learns about palate cleansers
m.how: Cut a pocket into 4 chicken breasts and fill with wilted spinach mixed with ricotta. Sear, then roast at 200C for 20 minutes. Bake a potato gratin alongside. Whisk lemon juice into melted butter and spoon over the chicken.

w.note: the sorbet Mia eats before she knows it's a palate cleanser
w.how: Simmer 2 sliced pears in water with a spoon of sugar for 8 minutes until tender, then cool. Scoop lemon sorbet into small chilled glasses and add a few pear slices and a mint leaf. Eat it neatly, and do not launch it across the table.

d.how: Fill glasses with ice. Pour in pear juice to halfway and top with cold sparkling water. Squeeze in a little lemon and stir once. The national drink of a kingdom famous for its pears.
